proof:
Use the preceding hollow graph's exact base and fibers. In one nonzero part, write its physical height map as $B_i p+L_i u+c_i$ in its auxiliary continuous coordinate $u$. On any positive full-dimensional auxiliary fiber it must be equal almost everywhere to the only allowed height $b(p)$, because the measure is a positive part of $\mu$. A nonzero linear functional is constant only on an affine hyperplane of volume zero in that dimension, so $L_i=0$ (automatic in dimension zero). Each part therefore has one affine height function of its base.

If total parity cost is at most eight, each of the eight parities must occur in exactly one part. The four parity-$000$ atoms at $0,2e_1,2e_2,2e_3$ must all have positive mass in one part. Their height zero forces that part's affine height to vanish. The auxiliary fibers above $2e_2,2e_3$ have a positive-volume midpoint inclusion by convexity and Brunn–Minkowski, or by nonemptiness in dimension zero, forcing positive mass above their midpoint $(0,1,1)$. Now that part is the unique one occupying parity $011$, so it must carry the atom at $r=(2,1,1)$ of height one. This contradicts the affine height zero.

For attainment take all five sites in $F$ with height $x/2$, all three sites of $[0,2e_1]$ with height zero, and four singleton parts at $e_2,e_3,e_1+e_2,e_1+e_3$. These are disjoint and cover $P$. Every part is lattice-complete in its own convex hull, by the face and site census. For each part with base hull $Q$, thicken $Q$ by the closed radius-$1/4$ ball in the orthogonal complement of the direction space of $\operatorname{aff}(Q)$. The thickened hull has nonempty interior in $\mathbb R^3$. Its intersection with $\operatorname{aff}(Q)$ is exactly $Q$. For the part on $F$ the affine plane is $y+z=2$ and an integer point off it has distance at least $1/\sqrt2$. For the line and singleton parts the distance of any off-span integer point is at least one. Thus thickening adds no integer site. Take the product of each thickened hull with a unit auxiliary interval and apply its displayed affine height map, extended to the ambient base. This gives a full-dimensional source body and unit mixed mass exactly at the part's original sites. The parity counts are $3,2,1,1,1,1$ and the affine base ranks are $2,1,0,0,0,0$. They give the two claimed costs.

statement: Let $P=(2\Delta_3\cap\mathbb Z^3)\cup\{(1,1,1),(2,1,1)\}$ and put $b=0$ on the simplex sites, $b(1,1,1)=1/2$, $b(2,1,1)=1$. Consider finite positive decompositions of $\mu=\sum_{p\in P}\delta_{(p,b(p))}$ in which each nonzero part is an affine pushforward, preserving the original base, of mixed ordinary volume on a convex body with positive full-dimensional auxiliary fibers at its positive bases. Let $k_i$ be that part's occupied parity count. The minimum of $\sum_i k_i$ is $9>8=k(P)$, allowing fractional allocations and varying auxiliary dimension, including dimension zero. There is a partition into parts with this parity cost whose sum of $2^{\text{affine base rank}}$ is ten.
title: A hollow atomic graph has exact original-base lift parity cost nine
